findings.reason: a node implementing §20 as written either writes a test that is red on the merged code (gate cannot pass) or changes `_guard_store()` to honor RECKON_HOME and breaks the `isolated_project` teardown; the section must instead anchor the expectation to the real home computed without the guard's own helper (for example derive it from `_config_home()` with RECKON_HOME removed, written out in the test), and its done-when must name a control that holds on the merged code.
findings.text: §20 says the test "sets `RECKON_HOME` to a temporary directory and expects the store at `<that directory>/crew`" and that its done-when "fails ... when `real_store_home()` ignores `RECKON_HOME`" while "It passes on the code as merged"; but the `real_store_home()` it names (tests/conftest.py, added by commit 1df24400f) does `override = os.environ.pop("RECKON_HOME", None)` before returning `_store._config_home()`, so it deliberately removes RECKON_HOME and returns the workstation's real home — `_guard_store()` (tests/test_member_friction.py:59, which returns `real_store_home()` when `RECKON_GUARD_HOME` is unset) therefore never yields a RECKON_HOME-derived path, and a test expecting `<that directory>/crew` fails on the merged code rather than passing. The two controls are mutually exclusive with the merged helper: the test fails on merged code, and the only way to make it pass is to have `_guard_store()` honor RECKON_HOME — which returns the fixture's own isolated home, so the teardown assertion `_assert_isolation(_guard_store())` in the `isolated_project` fixture (tests/test_member_friction.py:168) would fire on the fixture's own `state/sample/crew.json` roster, turning the suite red. The guard's whole purpose (its docstring: the escape destination a dispatcher reaches when it bypasses RECKON_HOME) requires it to resolve the real home independently of RECKON_HOME, so the proposed expectation contradicts the mechanism.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — commit `1df24400f` resolves and introduces `real_store_home()` and `real_store_is_not_a_fixture_target()` in tests/conftest.py as §20 states; `_guard_store()` exists at tests/test_member_friction.py:59; `_config_home()` at reckon/_store.py:128 resolves RECKON_HOME → ~/.config/reckon → ~/docs-server exactly as quoted; "score 99" resolves to the stored review `r-20261008T101343872035-review-of-picker-tests-read-their-own-state` (total 99).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §20's done-when names two measurable negative controls (the test must fail when `_guard_store()` returns a path literal, and when `real_store_home()` ignores `RECKON_HOME`) and states the passing arm; the defect is that the controls cannot hold together with the mechanism, which is scored under reasoning.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §20 writes only test files under tests/ and names no scratchpad or node-local path; its later reader opens tests/test_member_friction.py and tests/conftest.py in the repository.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §20 names no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into code; the commit hash and review score are evidence citations in the plan prose, not symbols.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the section's stated mechanism cannot produce its done-when on the code as merged, because the helper it builds the expectation around discards the very variable the expectation depends on.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §20 carries one deliverable: make the member-friction guard test compare against an expectation independent of the helper it exercises.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §20 declares no new depends-on edge and its dependency on §16 (the helpers it edits in tests/conftest.py) was raised and declined as redundant because §16 merges before §20 is dispatched; no relationship points at a wrong node.
